rationale: Write-level collaborator could call issue-tracker, wiki and mirror-sync endpoints reserved for repo admins; route guard was reqRepoWriter instead of reqRepoAdmin.
Unexpired session token of prebuilds system user persisted into claimed workspaces and was reusable; stale-credential/session lifecycle flaw, not a role or object decision on an operation.
Any authenticated user could delete reactions created by other users; handler lacked an ownership check. Same commit also fixed attachments, identity providers, registration.
Read-only collaborator could push via git-receive-pack by adding service=git-upload-pack to the query, because authorization used the client-supplied parameter rather than the RPC path.
Caller of the rotate endpoint could set a cluster-wide annotation in template metadata, widening a strict or namespace-scoped sealed secret to cluster-wide and enabling retargeting and decryption.
Suspended user's previously issued API key still passed authorization on AI Bridge proxy endpoints; account status was not checked. Operation not found in contract.
Non-admin operator could set allow_private on webhook subscriptions (create/update), a field reserved for admins, disabling the SSRF guard; handlers had no role check on that property.

Pull-mode agent credentials were bound to overly broad RBAC on the control plane, letting an authenticated agent gain admin-level access over other clusters; fix is role definitions in a CLI-provisioned setup.
Password-reset flow let users or admins with login restrictions (expired, disabled) reset a password and log in; login/reset-flow logic.
User with general write access could replace a process group adding restricted components, which require additional permission; framework skipped the restricted-component authorization on replace.
